title: Status snippets & subscriber summary — routing glitch communication kit
body:
Purpose:
This draft collects short, editable status-page snippets and a concise customer-facing summary template for a routing-related service disruption that affects model selection and request routing. Use this when the primary impact is: occasional 5xx/timeout responses, increased latencies for a subset of customers, or unexpected model routing to fallback variants. The goal is clarity, brevity, and clear remediation/next steps for downstream teams and paid customers.

Audience:
- External customers (engineering leads, platform owners) on our paid plans
- Customer Success and Account teams for customization
- Support engineers who will paste/update status page entries and outbound emails

Notes to SE/CS: keep language non-technical in public-facing text; include a short technical appendix only for customers who opt in. Always include a link to the incident timeline and an expected next update time.

Quick guidance (how to use):
- Pick one snippet per severity phase: INVESTIGATING / MITIGATING / MONITORING / RESOLVED
- Add one short line with customer-specific impact if known (e.g., "affects customers using model group X in us-west-2")
- Use the post-incident summary template after the incident is closed; include credits or remediation steps if applicable.

Status page snippets (short; < 280 chars each):
1) INVESTIGATING (initial):
"We are investigating increased errors and intermittent timeouts affecting request routing to some models. Our engineers are actively looking into the cause. We will post an update within 30 minutes. Impact: some requests may fail or be routed to fallback models."

2) MITIGATING (when workaround active):
"Mitigation in progress: we have applied a temporary routing rule to route affected requests to a compatible variant while we restore full routing. Latency may be higher and output may differ slightly. Teams affected: customers using pinned routing policies and model-group beta. ETA for full restore: TBD."

3) MONITORING (after fixes deployed):
"A fix has been deployed and we are monitoring traffic. Error rates have dropped substantially, but a small percentage of requests may see higher latency as caches repopulate. We expect normal behavior to resume within the next 2 hours."

4) RESOLVED (final brief):
"Service restored: routing logic returned to normal operation and error rates are at baseline. If you see lingering issues, please open a support ticket and reference RTE-412. A detailed customer-facing summary will be published shortly."

Short email template for high-touch customers (send within 2–4 hours of detection if impacted):
Subject: Update: temporary routing impact affecting Redwood inference (RTE-412)
Hi <Customer-Name>,
We wanted to notify you that earlier today we detected an issue that caused some requests to be routed to fallback model variants, resulting in increased errors or slight changes in output for a subset of traffic. Our engineers applied a mitigation and restored standard routing. We are continuing to monitor.
What happened (short): routing rules that map incoming requests to preferred model variants experienced an unexpected configuration drift when a deployment overlapped a throttling condition.
Customer impact: some requests returned 5xx or timeouts, and some completed responses came from a compatible fallback model. Affected: customers using model pinning and dynamic-routing in us-west-2 (estimate: ~6% of global requests).
Current status: mitigation applied; traffic is routing normally for most customers.
Next steps: we will run a rolling verification and publish a customer-facing summary with timeline and root cause within 72 hours. If you saw any production problems, tell us the request IDs and examples and we will prioritize support.
Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts production systems and appreciate your patience.
Best,
Sofia Martinez (on behalf of Customer Success & Engineering)

Customer-facing post-incident summary template (concise, 3 sections):
- Executive summary (1–2 sentences): what happened, when, who was affected, and current status. Keep it non-technical.
- Impact & timeline (bullet list): short timestamps (UTC) and customer-facing impact per interval (no internal task names).
- Resolution & next steps (bullets): what we fixed, what we will do to prevent recurrence, how we’ll compensate (if applicable), and where to find the full technical appendix.

Example filled template (for RTE-412):
Executive summary: On 2026-02-20 08:14 UTC we observed increased request failures and timeouts affecting model routing for a subset of customers in the us-west region. Impacted requests were routed to fallback variants or returned errors. Full routing behavior was restored by 2026-02-20 10:36 UTC. Customers using model pinning/dynamic routing experienced the majority of the impact.

Impact & timeline (UTC):
- 08:12 — First error spike detected by automated alerting (5xx + timeouts).
- 08:15 — Engineering triage initiated; initial mitigation (rate limit adjustment) attempted.
- 08:42 — Temporary routing rule enacted to route affected traffic to compatible variants (mitigation).
- 09:20 — Errors decreased but latency increased as caches repopulated.
- 10:36 — Routing control-plane rollback completed; routing returned to baseline.

Resolution & next steps:
- Root-cause (short): a control-plane race during a concurrent deployment caused stale route state to be applied under throttling conditions, producing incorrect model selection.
- Fix applied: rollback of the deployment, hotfix to prevent stale route application, and expanded guardrails in the control-plane logic.
- Preventative actions: add pre-deploy validation to detect stale route state, increase control-plane throttling visibility in dashboards, and a post-deploy quick verification for pinned routing customers.
- Customer remediation: we are offering 1% credit on February usage for impacted accounts; CS will follow up for accounts with measurable business impact.

Technical appendix (optional; include link only in the public doc): provide deeper details for engineering contacts willing to review stack traces, deployment IDs, and exact request examples. Link: confluence://incident/routing-glitch-2026-02

FAQ snippets (for Support/CS to paste):
Q: Will outputs differ if requests were routed to fallback variants?
A: In most cases fallback variants are functionally compatible but may produce subtle differences in wording and, rarely, slight latency changes. If output fidelity is critical we will help re-run requests on the restored model where feasible.

Q: What should customers do now?
A: Monitor your application for increased latency/errors. If you see production impact, collect example request IDs and timestamps and open a support ticket referencing JIRA-RTE-412. CS will prioritize remediation.

Open questions / to-do (internal):
- Confirm exact percent of traffic affected per customer (Billing/Telemetry) — action: Maya to run per-customer query by EOD.
- Draft final customer-specific remediation notes for top 10 impacted accounts — action: Drew + CS.
- Confirm credit calculation and legal sign-off — action: Finance/Legal.

Checklist before publishing final summary:
- Include verified timestamps and request samples (ops)
- Attach customer impact table for high-touch accounts (CS)
- Legal approval for any credits (Finance/Legal)
